title: POC field guide: model chooser + quant experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a working field guide for customer POCs where we need to pick a model footprint, quantization profile, and prompt/pipeline tuning strategy that meets SLOs for latency and cost while preserving acceptable quality. Focus: getting to a repeatable set of microbenchmarks + recipes that SEs can reuse across retail and finserv pilots.

Context and constraints:
- Customer baseline: semi-structured product data + retrieval layer, target 95th latency < 600ms for single-turn completions, cost target <$0.003 per call for standard queries.
- Deployment: usually Redwood Dedicated for pilots, occasionally Private (VPC). We assume our serving runtime features: prefix KV cache, continuous batching, and kernel selection per hardware.
- Failure/fallback budget: allowed to fallback to a smaller model for 10% of requests if larger model capacity saturated.

Quick checklist before experiments:
- Confirm tokenizer behavior on customer prompt corpus (out-of-vocab tokens, tokenization blowup).
- Create 300–500 representative prompts (mix of short queries, long-context multi-doc prompts, and edge cases).
- Capture reference outputs from a high-quality baseline (fp16 LLM on hosted infra) for evaluation.
- Instrument tracing hooks (request_id, model_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_hit).

Experiment matrix (recommended sweep order):
1) Tokenizer sanity: run full prompt corpus through tokenizer across candidate models. Flag prompts where token count differs > 15% between models.
2) Model selection sweep (quality proxy + perf): candidate models = Mistral-7B-instruct, Llama2-13B (hybrid), Falcon-40B-instruct-lite (non-commercial customers only), and one distilled 7B variant. For each model: run 1000 synthetic queries at cold start and warmed (cache primed) conditions.
3) Quantization sweep: for each model, test fp16 (baseline), int8, q4-style 4-bit (if supported by runtime), and a conservative 6-bit profile. Measure perplexity drift on a small held-out set and end-task metric (F1/ROUGE/BLEU depending on task).
4) Batch & latency sweep: test batch sizes 1, 2, 4 for tail-latency behavior. Capture P50/P95/P99 and average tokens/sec.
5) Prefix caching / KV priming tests: run typical conversational prefixes through cache and measure token savings and latency improvements for subsequent queries.
6) Mixed routing test: route 80% requests to smaller quantized model and 20% to larger fp16 for quality-sensitive queries. Measure user-facing quality delta vs cost savings.

Microbench setup notes:
- Use a synthetic load generator with realistic inter-arrival times. Don’t hammer with perfect concurrency; include jitter.
- Warm-up: run 50 representative prompts to populate prefix cache before measurement phase.
- For fairness, pin sequence length to 512 in primary sweep (matches customer median). Run edge-case at 2048 to validate fallback.
- Record hardware: gpu type, CUDA version, runtime kernel set. Note any kernel fallbacks observed in traces.

Sample results summary (example from retail pilot X):
- Mistral-7B instruct int8: P95 = 380ms, cost/call = $0.0019, relative quality drop ~4% vs fp16 baseline on product QA task.
- Llama2-13B fp16: P95 = 720ms (exceeds SLO), but Q eval higher by ~7 points; when quantized to q4_0-like profile on our runtime: P95 = 490ms, cost/call = $0.0036, quality delta ~2%.
- Falcon-40B-lite q4: P95 = 640ms (marginal), high memory churn caused occasional kernel fallback, manifested as 1–2s spikes.
- Hybrid routing (80/20 Mistral/Llama13): avg cost/call = $0.0023, P95 = 420ms, task metric within 1.2% of baseline.

Interpretation & heuristics:
- If customer SLO is tight (< 500ms P95) and quality requirement is moderate, prefer a quantized 7B-class model (Mistral/distil) with int8 or conservative 4-bit.
- If quality is top priority and customer accepts higher tail latencies, use 13B fp16 with careful batching and autoscaling; quantize only after validating output regressions on a prompt set.
- Avoid 40B-class models in Dedicated if GPU memory is marginal on node type; they introduce kernel fallback spikes that are hard to predict.
- Prefetch/prefix-caching yields best ROI when >30% of requests share prefixes (chat/history domination).

Prompt & pipeline tuning notes:
- Prompt compression: rewrite retrieval + instruction into a compact system message; strip filler text. Measure token savings vs any quality regression.
- Multi-stage pipeline: retrieval -> condensed prompt -> model -> reranker. Reranker can be run on a small distilled model to reduce calls to the big model.
- Use few-shot exemplars sparingly; 3 exemplars often enough for classification-style tasks. For generative, prefer 1 exemplar + strong system instruction.
- For hallucination-prone tasks, add an explicit "cite source" constraint and post-filter using fuzzy match to retrieved docs.

Quality evaluation approach:
- Use a mixture of automated metrics and 50–100 human evals (quick check) on high-risk prompts.
- Track per-prompt regressions and classify by failure mode: omission, fabrication, wrong attribute. Maintain a small golden prompt set per customer for regression alerts.

Operational suggestions for POC runs:
- Canary rollout for quantized model on 5% of traffic with detailed logging. If regression rate > 6% (customer-defined), rollback to baseline.
- Implement model-variant headers in responses for product teams to trace which variant produced an answer.
- Keep an "escape hatch" route: if KV prefix cache hit ratio drops below 15% and P95 climbs, temporarily route to higher-capacity pool.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Need a standardized metric set for "acceptable quality drop" per vertical (retail vs finserv). Assign: Priya to draft (JIRA-RW-1520).
- Kernel fallback incidents: get SRE trace correlation for Falcon-40B spikes — Ethan to open issue with infra team.
- Confirm legal/commercial constraints for Falcon model use with customer A (Marco to confirm).

Appendix (quick commands & artifacts):
- Tokenizer checks: python scripts/tokenizer_probe.py --model $MODEL --corpus prompts.json
- Microbench harness: ./bench/run_load.py --target $REDWOOD_HOST --model $MODEL --batch 1 --seq 512 --warmup 50 --duration 600
- Evaluation: tools/eval_harness.py --gold gold.json --candidates outdir/ --metrics rouge,f1,exact_match

Notes to SEs: keep experiment logs (traces + perf CSVs) attached to JIRA ticket. When in doubt start with Mistral-7B-int8-like profiles as they tend to hit the best latency/cost sweet spot for conversational retail workloads.
